D20·ay1j — 2026-09-22
rule: Never treat the evaluator's caps as covering spend outside a cells root — work that runs outside one carries its own stated accounting, and an unreported cost is recorded in the units it was observed in, never as an invented total.
chose: The caps enforce only what they can SEE, and that is a standing property of the D12/D17 machinery, not a one-off (sofar-c3, 2026-09-22). Two proofs from tonight. (1) BLIND BY PATH: roundClaudeSpend read only ~IO/bench-cells/boopada, so round 2's /Users/Shared smoke ledgers were invisible until c562789. The since-reset figure moved $124.69 → $160.61 the moment they became visible; that jump was accounting catching up, never new spending. (2) BLIND BY LOCATION: drive-visibility 5.1 ran in a session scratchpad outside every cells root, so no evaluator cap can ever see it. It is real usage in the same 5-hour window and week. Therefore: any future work that spends outside a cells root states its own accounting in the record, and a cost the adapter never reported is written in the units actually observed ("6 short haiku sessions"), with the estimate labelled as scale and never folded into a total. The one place the true figure exists is the provider's usage view, which no session here can read; asking the operator is the only way to obtain it. A follow-up is queued, not done: put this property in a comment at roundClaudeSpend in the evaluator's lib/ledger.ts. It cannot be done while cycle-L11b runs — D18 makes a moved evaluator HEAD throw mid-run and a dirty tree refuse the next launch — so it waits for the cycle to end.
over: (a) Inventing a dollar figure for 5.1 from comparable haiku sessions and folding it into the budget picture. A made-up number cannot be told from a measured one later and cannot be removed. (b) Leaving the property in a passing note, where the next session reading the cap code would not meet it. (c) Widening the caps to scan the whole filesystem for ledgers, which would make the arithmetic unpredictable and still miss work that keeps no ledger, such as 5.1.
because: A cap that silently omits a spend source reads as authoritative while being wrong, which is worse than one whose blind spots are named. Naming both blind spots — by path and by location — tells a future session which question to ask before trusting a number, and keeps the honest gap visible until the operator can close it from the usage view.
